messages:
Marta L: Quick flag — Feb invoice shows us-central1 (ORD) GPU $/hr materially above other regions. It looks like committed hours are idle while on-demand fills peaks. Can someone sanity-check? :eyes:

Ash K: Which BI view did you pull? Need the per-region breakdown and reserved_util numbers to triage.

Marta L: Pasting the lightweight extract I grabbed from billing (rounded):
``` 
region        | eff_gpu_hour | reserved_util | avg_inst_util | egress_tb
---------------------------------------------------------------
us-west-2     | $5.10        | 0.62          | 76%           | 1.8
us-east-1     | $5.40        | 0.75          | 80%           | 2.1
us-central1   | $7.20        | 0.38          | 59%           | 3.0   <-- ORD
eu-west-1     | $4.85        | 0.68          | 72%           | 1.2
```

Billing Bot: Alert: Reserved GPU utilization below threshold in us-central1. Potential SKU mismatch or orphaned reservations. Ticket BILL-4992 created.

Devon: We did a placement tweak last month to rebalance dedicated pools. Some latency-sensitive endpoints were pinned to ORD because partner infra had lower hop. That might explain why on-demand is topping.

Samir: Two signals I saw in cluster logs: (1) batch reranker jobs spilled from us-west into us-central during peak windows, (2) cross-region model fetches increased, adding egress and remote KV latency.

Jing: Finance context: a 1y regional commit on H100 equiv in us-central1 is ~-30% list. But unused commit hours are cash burn. If reserved_util < 50% we should not be holding that size of commit there.

Ash K: Proposed immediate steps:
- 48h forensic: tag-level billing join, pod->node->region mapping, autoscaler event window
- Temporarily cap autoscaler max in us-central1 to prevent on-demand surge while we investigate
- 7-day canary: shift non-critical batch rerankers to eu-west-1 spot pools and measure impact

Marta L: I can run the 48h forensic. Will join billing tags to kubernetes metadata and include autoscaler events. Expect first CSVs in ~4h. Opening INFRA-2428 to track.

Devon: +1 on capping. Also check instance families — we've accidentally been mixing vCPU-heavy node types in ORD that were intended for CPU workloads. Right-sizing should help reserved_util and net cost.

Samir: For the canary, enable a short TTL local model cache to reduce cross-region pulls. That will cut egress and reduce accidental spill to ORD.

Jing: When Marta posts the forensic I need two numbers: (A) reserved_util vs 7-day peak baseline, (B) estimated savings if we move X% of batch to eu-west-1. I can draft commit-ROI tables from that.

Marta L: Query snippet I'll run: `SELECT region, sum(gpu_hours) AS hours, reserved_hours FROM billing WHERE date >= '2026-02-01' GROUP BY region;` Adding this to INFRA-2428.

Ash K: Who owns the 48h forensic? Need tag-level joins and autoscaler events from 02/08 00:00 -> 02/10 00:00.

Marta L: I'll own it. Will attach `kubectl get nodes -o wide`, autoscaler events logs, and pod->node mappings.

Devon: After numbers, run the 7-day reranker canary to eu-west1 spot pools. Measure p50/p95, error rate, and egress delta. If safe, proceed to resize commit and apply autoscaler caps.

Samir: Also watch co-scheduling: nodes with idle vCPU seats have been blocking cheaper instance families. Add a CPU/GPU co-scheduling check to the forensic.

Billing Bot: BILL-4992 linked -> INFRA-2428. Reserved SKU IDs flagged for review.

Jing: If forensic shows >30% wasted reserved hours, I'll recommend immediate resize on renewal and discuss a temporary finance credit for last-month overspend.

Marta L: Dump will be in INFRA-2428 in ~4h. I'll also open INFRA-2429 to PR an autoscaler cap (baseline +10%).

Infra Bot: Created actions: INFRA-2428 (forensic), INFRA-2429 (autoscaler cap PR), INFRA-2430 (eu-west1 reranker canary). Please assign owners in ticket comments.

Ash K: Thanks — once forensic lands I'll draft a short runbook: cap -> canary -> commit resize -> caching tweak -> monitor 14 days.

Marta L: Thanks all. I'll post the CSVs and a brief summary in the ticket. :rocket:
